svg.title: Operating modes
svg.text: How a batch moves through the phases
A: each tunnel runs the whole cycle in place, staggered 5 days apart (base design). B: a loader moves each batch from tunnel to tunnel.
▼ loader empties one tunnel to the maturation hall and refills it, every 5 days. The batch never moves inside.
B TRANSFER BETWEEN TUNNELS (one phase per tunnel)
▼ every 5 days: empty T-103, move T-102 → T-103 and T-101 → T-102 (hot, open-air moves), refill T-101.
Batch = 196 t (230 m³) of fresh feedstock. In A it fills a tunnel to 2.8 m and settles to 1.3 m by day 15.
Phases drawn as 5-day blocks for clarity; the control setpoints are in CE-10.
Recommendation: A as the base design
Half the loader work, no hot material in the open, identical tunnels.
The patent's one-chamber-per-phase idea survives as a control scheme:
each tunnel passes through the phases in time instead of in space.
B is worth a pilot trial only if remixing at day 5 and 10 proves
to raise the temperature or the heat recovered.
Assumptions in model/compost_energy/industrial.py (Handling): 0.25 L diesel/t, 120 t/h, 10 K lost per hot move, 30 % mass loss over 15 days. Routine fill/empty is inside the €100k operating cost.
